finding_against_codex.severity: auditability — not a release-blocking safety hole
finding_against_codex.defect: A candidate whose code is not on the production allowlist is `continue`d — it is recorded in NEITHER tags NOR abstentions. HP@0.72 and MT@0.99 vanish with no record anywhere.
finding_against_codex.why_it_matters: This contradicts the function's own docstring two lines above: 'A candidate below its floor is recorded as an abstention, never dropped. Silence and uncertainty are different facts and auditors need to tell them apart.' A reader of an assertion cannot distinguish (a) HP was evaluated and withheld by release policy, (b) HP was never evaluated, (c) HP evaluated and found nothing. It is the same collapse-of-distinct-states pattern as the UNK overload corrected in RFC-0004, reappearing one layer down — and it defeats the auditability that is the allowlist's purpose.
finding_against_codex.proposed_fix: a third return bucket, e.g. `policy_suppressed: [{code, confidence, floor, reason: 'not_on_production_allowlist'}]`, so the record states that HP fired at 0.72 and was withheld by policy. Owner: Codex (services/).
finding_against_codex.test_gap: tests/test_release_policy.py::test_gateway_rejects_nonproduction_even_at_full_confidence asserts rejection but does not assert that a record of the suppression exists.
